subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should trusted hook-agent integrations get an explicit persistent session mode, or should `/hooks/agent` remain isolated-only with docs clarifying that stable `sessionKey` is metadata routing rather than transcript continuity?
rationale: Current code proves the requested behavior is missing, but the fix changes hook API/config surface and session security boundaries, so maintainers need to confirm the permanent product contract before closing the issue.

options.title: Accept explicit persistent mode
options.body: Review and land a narrow version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 that preserves isolated default behavior and gates persistent reuse through existing hook auth and session-key policy.

options.title: Keep hook agents isolated-only
options.body: Close or reject the linked PR direction and update docs to state that `/hooks/agent` cannot preserve transcript continuity through `sessionKey`.

options.title: Choose a different identity model
options.body: Defer the PR and design a broader deterministic session identity model for trusted hooks before adding public config surface.

recommendation.title: Accept explicit persistent mode
recommendation.body: Review and land a narrow version of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75918 that preserves isolated default behavior and gates persistent reuse through existing hook auth and session-key policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter supplied the most recent product-direction comment for this exact issue and is the best available owner for the API/security choice.
